findings.title: A fixed host's date override does not require the whole slot to fit
findings.body: Once an override date is found, this logic only rejects a slot whose start is after the override end; it never rejects a slot that starts before the override end but finishes after it. For example, a 60-minute slot from 17:30 to 18:30 is accepted for an override ending at 18:00. Such a slot can be generated from a loose round-robin host's availability and then incorrectly remain bookable even though the fixed host cannot attend. The check needs to require slotStartTime >= override start and slotEndTime <= override end using consistent half-open boundaries.

findings.title: Working-hours validation treats no matching interval as available
findings.body: The predicate searches for any working-hours interval that the slot is outside of, rather than requiring an interval that contains the slot. If a fixed host has no working-hours row on that weekday, find() returns undefined and the host is treated as available. It also rejects every slot for a host with split hours: a 10:00 slot in a 09:00-12:00 interval is rejected because it is outside the separate 13:00-17:00 interval. In a round-robin event, slots generated by a loose host can therefore be offered while a fixed host is unavailable, or valid fixed-host slots can all disappear. This should use a positive containment check over the host's intervals.

findings.title: Working-hours validation ignores the booking duration
findings.body: Both start and end are calculated from slotStartTime, so the condition only checks whether the slot starts within a fixed host's working hours. A one-hour slot beginning at 11:30 for a host working until 12:00 passes this check even though it ends at 12:30. Although getTimeSlots normally constrains the host that generated a candidate, a loose round-robin host can generate this candidate and this new fixed-host filter is then responsible for rejecting it. Calculate end from slotEndTime and require the complete slot to fit.

findings.title: Override timezone conversion is adjusted a second time across DST
findings.body: The override minutes are already translated using the organizer and invitee offsets at the override timestamp, but buildSlots subsequently adds organizerDSTDiff - inviteeDSTDiff based on the current date and the invitee day. This shifts date overrides by an hour whenever the override date has a different DST offset than today. For example, when evaluated in January, a 10:00 America/New_York override in July for a UTC invitee is converted here to 14:00, then buildSlots applies the -60 minute organizer DST difference and produces 13:00. Date overrides are dated absolute exceptions and must not receive the recurring-working-hours DST correction again.

findings.title: Equal override endpoints are compared by object identity
findings.body: Each dayjs(...).add(...) call creates a distinct Dayjs object, so strict equality is always false even when date.start and date.end represent the same instant. The special handling for a zero-length/all-day-unavailable override therefore never runs. A candidate that starts exactly at that instant can fall through to dateOverrideExist and be considered available; compare the timestamps with isSame() instead.

findings.title: The claimed fixed-host round-robin behavior has no regression coverage
findings.body: The added timezone assertion exercises a regular one-user event only. It does not create a ROUND_ROBIN event with a fixed host, a loose host whose availability generates the candidate slot, and a fixed-host date override. The existing round-robin test also has no fixed hosts. Consequently the new fixed-host filtering path, including the case this PR is intended to prevent, is untested and the overbooking and split-availability regressions can merge unnoticed.
